name: North Chimney
text: [overview] Often written off as a miserable approach to The Diamond over loose rock in summer, or loose snow in winter, yet in spring it becomes a decent mixed route.
[overview] It starts as an obvious snow gully rising to Broadway and grows steadily more difficult, with the steepest drytooling on the final pitch.
[overview] Move left at the end, hack a way across a snow flute, and roll onto Broadway.
[approach] Continue past the lake to Mills Glacier.

[approach] The chimney is right of center on the lower east face, directly below Broadway and the Diamond, and follows the large left-slanting chimney above the highest snow on the face other than Lamb's Slide.
[descent_text] The rappel line from Broadway leads to Mills Glacier and needs two ropes.
